state: A 32-year-old woman has keratoconus with documented progression over the past year. Her astigmatism has increased and topography shows progressive steepening. Pachymetry is 440 µm. The plan is to use the standard Dresden protocol for epithelium-off cross-linking: remove the epithelium, apply riboflavin 0.1% every 5 minutes for 30 minutes, and expose to UV-A 3 mW/cm² for 30 minutes. The question is whether this plan can proceed without modification.

state: A 64-year-old woman is reviewed on the oculoplastic ward two days after admission for a periorbital soft tissue infection. A deep tissue sample taken at the bedside has already shown fascial necrosis with gram-positive cocci in chains, so the diagnosis is established. Despite this, the surgical team has not yet defined how far the infection extends: it is unclear whether the process involves the orbital septum, the deep fascial planes or the sinus cavity, whether gas is present, and where the infection began. The patient remains febrile and hypotensive and is receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics, clindamycin and fluid resuscitation. Debridement has been scheduled for the next few hours and the operating surgeon has asked for anatomical information to plan the extent of tissue removal. No visual deficit is recorded.

Fundus examination shows a featureless retina with a poor foveal reflex, retinal arteriolar narrowing, only minimal dot hemorrhages and microaneurysms, no exudates or cotton-wool spots, and no active neovascularization; a chronic neovascular frond with surrounding fibrovascular tissue in the superior arcade has been stable for several months. Extensive panretinal photocoagulation scarring is present in both eyes. SD-OCT shows a central subfield thickness of 204 µm without intraretinal cysts, so there is no central-involved macular edema. Macular capillary perfusion has never been imaged in either eye. She has hypertension treated with amlodipine.

state: A 7-year-old boy is brought for drooping of the right upper eyelid and double vision that began two days after the onset of a severe right periorbital headache. He has had similar headaches twice in the past year. On examination there is complete ptosis OD, limited elevation, depression and adduction OD, and a dilated right pupil with a sluggish reaction to light. Visual acuity and fundus examination are normal. There is no proptosis, no orbital bruit, no fever and no weight loss. He has no known diabetes and no history of malignancy. No imaging has been obtained and there is no history of trauma. He is otherwise well, afebrile, and neurologically intact apart from the right third nerve.

He reports no eye pain, has never undergone ocular surgery, and has not used topical antimetabolites. Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/200 bilaterally. On slit-lamp examination a narrow rim of iris remnant is seen, the central cornea is clear, and only the inferior peripheral cornea OS shows mild thickening with early vascularization and punctate epithelial staining. There is no central corneal opacification and no keratinisation. Tear film breakup time is shortened. The lens is transparent and the anterior chamber is quiet. These peripheral corneal changes have been unchanged for a year.

state: A 58-year-old man is being followed for a right corneal ulcer that began two weeks after cataract surgery. Smears from a corneal scraping showed gram-positive, branching, beaded filaments that stained with a modified acid-fast stain, and cultures on blood agar, chocolate agar and Sabouraud dextrose agar grew tiny white dry colonies within 48 to 72 hours. The organism has not yet been identified to species level and susceptibility results are not available. The clinical picture is consistent with the laboratory findings: a midperipheral anterior stromal infiltrate with an overlying epithelial defect and satellite lesions, a 2 mm hypopyon, and no corneal thinning or extension beyond the limbus. Visual acuity is 20/80, intraocular pressure is 14 mmHg and the posterior segment is normal. Topical amikacin has been started and he is reviewed daily.

A pre-operative intranasal endoscopic examination shows a marked septal deviation to the right with hypertrophic middle turbinates, and the endoscopist reports that there is not enough space to place the tube safely. The eyelids and medial canthal tissues are normal, with no prior tarsorrhaphy or traumatic deformity. No septoplasty has been performed. The planned procedure is endoscopic conjunctivodacryocystorhinostomy with placement of a glass tube. She is otherwise healthy and takes no ocular medications. All findings above were recorded before the planned procedure.

amd_stage_od.instructions: Classify the right eye on the Beckman clinical classification of age-related macular degeneration (based on lesions within two disc diameters of the fovea).
criteria: No apparent ageing changes: no drusen and no AMD pigmentary abnormalities
Normal ageing changes: only small drusen (63 um or smaller) and no AMD pigmentary abnormalities
Early AMD: medium drusen (larger than 63 um and 125 um or smaller) and no AMD pigmentary abnormalities
Intermediate AMD: large drusen (larger than 125 um) and/or any AMD pigmentary abnormalities
